about: As the water is blessed and poured into the chalice of wine, the priest asks that through the mystery of this water and wine we may share in the divinity of Christ, who deigned to share our humanity. The prayer praises God, who wonderfully created the dignity of human nature and yet more wonderfully restored it. In Masses for the Dead the prayer is said and the water is not blessed.

seg.nr: The priest makes the sign of the cross with the paten and places the Host on the corporal. The deacon supplies the wine and the subdeacon the water. At low Mass the priest pours both and blesses the water with the sign of the cross.

seg.tr: God, You wondrously created the dignity of human nature and restored it still more wondrously. Through the mystery of this water and wine, grant us a share in the divinity of Jesus Christ, Your Son, our Lord, who deigned to share in our humanity and, being God, lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit for ever and ever. Amen.

ex.w027: Latin “dignátus est” uses two words. English likewise needs the auxiliary in “didst vouchsafe”.

seg.nr: In Masses for the Dead the prayer is said, but the water is not blessed.
